# A `map` over a `filter`, in a function of an instance built at run time, on
# every target.
#
# On the Go targets each becomes a loop filling a list, and the second ranges
# over the first's. fyne and gtk4 read any name a pass made that a loop
# ranges over as a field of the receiver -- right for a slot's list, which
# the instance declares -- so the second loop ranged over `c.__list0`, a field
# no record has, and the program did not build. A pass's own local is read as
# the local it is.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import ui "sngl:ui"
import test "sngl:test"

component card(base int) ui.node {
    var n = 2

    // The doubled values of those above one.
    func doubled() list[int] {
        return [base, n, n + 1].filter(func(x int) => x > 1).map(func(x int) => x * 2)
    }

    ui.text(value="{doubled().length()}")
}

component main ui.node {
    var shown = false

    ui.button #show(text="show", @click { shown = true })
    if shown {
        card #c(base=1)
    }
}

func testDoubles(t test.Test, c main) {
    c.show.click()
    t.assert(c.c != null && c.c.doubled().length() == 2)
}
